name: MatrixOne
tagline: MySQL-compatible cloud-native HTAP database on object storage, with vector search and snapshots.
description: MatrixOne is an open-source hyper-converged database from MatrixOrigin, written in Go. It separates stateless compute nodes from a shared log service and object storage (S3-compatible), and uses a single columnar storage format for both transactional and analytical queries, aiming to replace a MySQL plus warehouse combination with one engine. It speaks the MySQL protocol, supports vector types and indexes for AI retrieval, and offers snapshots and point-in-time restore that act like time travel for data. MatrixOrigin also runs a managed MatrixOne Cloud. Adoption is concentrated in China and the project is younger than TiDB or OceanBase, so evaluate maturity carefully.

pricing.notes: Open source and free to self-host; MatrixOne Cloud is billed by usage.

scale.notes: Compute nodes scale independently over shared object storage; log service replicated with Raft.

strengths: One engine for transactional and analytical queries over columnar storage
Compute/storage separation on cheap object storage
MySQL protocol compatibility for existing tools
Vector types and indexes for AI retrieval in SQL
Snapshots and PITR for data recovery
weaknesses: Young project with frequent breaking changes between releases
MySQL compatibility gaps (no triggers or stored procedures)
Point-write latency higher than row-store OLTP databases
useCases: Consolidating MySQL plus a warehouse into one HTAP engine
IoT and time-series ingestion with analytics
RAG applications needing vectors and SQL together
notIdealFor: Mission-critical OLTP needing long production track record
Apps relying on MySQL triggers or procedures
